units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 6:1">B. Kam. VI, 1</cite> <he>נ׳ בפניה כראוי</he> if he locked it in (secured the flock) properly.

<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Batra 2:11">Tosef. B. Bath. II, 11</cite>, a. e. <he>נ׳ וגדר וכ׳</he> if he fastened (something on the property), fenced in or tore down, it is possession (<cite ref="H00556"><he>חֲזָקָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 13:6">Sabb. XIII, 6</cite> <he>ונ׳ אחד בפניו</he> and one blocked it (by placing himself in the entrance).

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 13:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>לנוֹעֵל את ביתו וכ׳</he> it is like one locking up (sitting at the entrance of) his house to guard it. Mekh. Mishp. s. 18 <he>שלא לִנְעוֹל בפני וכ׳</he> in order not to close the door to future proselytes (not to discourage them on account of advanced age).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 32a">Snh. 32ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כדי שלא תִנְעוֹל וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00864"><he>דֶּלֶת</he></cite>.—Y. Naz. VIII, 57ᵃ bot., v. <cite ref="F00071"><he>וַעַד</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 5:9">Tosef. Sot. V, 9</cite> [read:] <he>שנעל דלת וכ׳</he> who locked his wife up (to prevent her from going astray); Y. ib. I, 17ᵃ bot.; <cite ref="Gittin 90a">Gitt. 90ᵃ</cite>; Y. Kidd. IV, 66ᵃ; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:2">Cant. R. to VII, 2</cite> (play on <he>בנעלים</he>, <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:2">ib.</cite>) <he>אתם נוֹעֲלִים לפני … ואני נועל וכ׳</he> you lock up (interrupt business) for my sake on Passover …, and I lock up (the rain) for your sake, v. <cite ref="N00979"><he>נְעִילָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מה היה … שהיו נועלין בעד כל הצרות</he> how great wa is the beauty of thy steps (pilgrimage to the Temple) which locked up (protected against) all troubles.—Part. pass. <he>נְעוּל</he>; f. <he>נְעוּלָה</he>; pl. <cite ref="N00972"><he>נְעוּלִים</he></cite>, <he>נְעוּלִין</he>; <he>נְעוּלוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 4:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. IV</cite> <he>שערי תפלה … נ׳ וכ׳</he> the gates of prayer are sometimes open, sometimes closed, but the gates of tears are never closed; a. e.

senses.gloss: to tie a sandal, to put shoes on.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 4:8">Tosef. Sabb. IV</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 5:8">V</cite>), 8 <he>לא יִנְעוֹל אדם וכ׳</he> one must not put on a nail-studded sandal &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7:16">Y. M. Kat. III, 83ᶜ</cite> <he>הורי</he> … <he>לנעול בו ביום</he> R. … allowed (the people mourning for R. Yassa) to wear shoes on the same day.
Tosef. Kidd. I, 5 נ׳ לו סנדלו וכ׳ if the slave tied his sandals for him (the new master) or untied them, it is possession (v. supra); B. Bath. 53ᵇ (Ms. M. הִנְעִיל); a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab., shod.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 7:2">Yalk. Josh. 7</cite> <he>וכי במנעלים אתה נ׳ וכ׳</he> dost thou wear shoes and observest not mourning?

senses.gloss: to put shoes on a person. B. Bath. l. c.; Kidd. 22ᵇ הלבישו הִנְעִילוֹ וכ׳ if the slave helped him put on his clothes or his shoes or lifted him up (helped him into a conveyance), it is possession.

units: <cite ref="Berakhot 32b:5">Ber. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>מיום … נִנְעֲלוּ שערי וכ׳</he> since the day the Temple was destroyed, the gates of prayer have been closed.
<cite ref="Berakhot 32b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>שערי דמעה לא ננעלו</he>; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 4:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. IV</cite> <he>נִנְעָלִים</he>, v. supra.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 59a:7">B. Mets. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>כל השערים נִנְעָלִים חוץ וכ׳</he> all gates (of prayer) are (at times) closed, except the gates for the cry of oppression.
<cite ref="Eruvin 6b">Erub. 6ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>אילמלא דלתותיה נִנְעָלוֹת</he> if its gates were not shut by night; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 67a:18">Sabb. 67ᵃ</cite> bot. (in an incantation for a swallowed fish-bone) <he>נִנְעַלְתָּה כתריס</he> (Ms. M. <he>מנעלתה בתריס</he>) thou art locked up as (within) a cuirass.
